# GripConstraint.Moves

**Enum** · namespace `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · assembly `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Runtime/Scripts/Interaction/GripConstraint.cs#L26)

What a constraint moves when the hand works it.

```csharp
public enum GripConstraint.Moves
```

## Fields

### TheObject {#theobject}

`TheObject = 0`

The grabbable itself. A door, a drawer, a valve, a power cell drawn out of its socket -
anything where the thing you are holding is the thing that travels. Driven through the
hold, so the object resists, takes contacts and can be stopped by the world.

### ThisPart {#thispart}

`ThisPart = 1`

Only this grip point and whatever hangs off it, relative to the object it sits on. A
shotgun's foregrip, a bolt, a charging handle, a slide - a part that travels along
something that is itself being carried.

A part is a transform rather than a body, so it is placed rather than simulated: the
world cannot stop it and only its own limits can. That is what a real mechanism does,
and it is the only way the object stays carryable - a rail measured from where the
object rests pins the object to that rail, which is right for a door bolted to a wall
and wrong for a gun in the player's hands.
